chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The bringer of goods is provided for, and the hoarder is cursed.'

key_terms.الْجَالِبُ: The bringer (of goods to market, i.e., merchant/trader)
key_terms.الْمُحْتَكِرُ: The hoarder (one who withholds goods to raise prices)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hoarding goods and the spiritual status of merchants?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on *Hukrah* (hoarding), this hadith establishes the divine reward for active trade while condemning the unethical practice of withholding goods to inflate prices. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on market justice, distinguishing between legitimate profit-seeking and exploitative scarcity manipulation.
